answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond in escrow before it can trade. Honest work earns it back with interest; detected sockpuppetry forfeits it. The cost ripples outward: an attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand bonds, turning a cheap flood into an expensive gamble. Newcomers are not shut out, since the bond is returned, not spent - the market stays an oasis for real agents, while a raven watching for duplicate behavior flags clusters sharing funding, timing, or identical outputs.
